newsitem.title: JAPAN: Mitsui Mining says acted at M'bishi Oil's request.
newsitem.headline: Mitsui Mining says acted at M'bishi Oil's request.

text.p: Mitsui Mining Co Ltd's executive managing director Shuji Nishino said on Friday his company paid money to an Osaka-based oil dealer through transactions at the request of Mitsubishi Oil Co Ltd.
"We acted upon Mitsubishi Oil's request, this will become clear in the courts," Nishino said.

Asked if he thought the transactions with Mitsubishi Oil were a little murky, Nishino said: "We thought they were a bit unclear, however, we responded because Mitsubishi Oil said they would guarantee it (would be safe)."
Nishino told reporters he had no knowledge of whether the money Mitsui Mining paid the dealer ended up being used as political contributions.
The oil products trader, Junichi Izui, was arrested on Thursday on suspicion of evading 320 million yen ($2.85 million) in taxes.
Local media have reported that Izui had close political ties and made donations to several legislators from the Liberal Democratic Party, which formed a minority government on Thursday.
Earlier on Friday, Tokyo prosecutors raided the headquarters of Mitsui Mining Co. The headquarters of Mitsubishi Oil were raided by prosecutors on Thursday.
Nishino said Tokyo prosecutors are questioning senior officials of Mitsui Mining, but he declined to identify them or to provide other details.
Nishino said he and the vice president of Mitsui Mining had previously met Izui.
Nishino said he met Izui in August 1995 when the oil products dealer said he could not meet payment commitments. Nishino said his firm has had no dealing with Izui since then.
Because of the dispute, Mitsui Mining has considerably scaled back its transactions in the domestic spot oil products market, Nishino said.
"Compared to when our business in domestic oil products peaked in 1994, that type of business has fallen to half," Nishino said.
He said Mitsui Mining's business in oil products peaked at three million kilolitres in the 1994/95 fiscal year.
In a suit filed in Tokyo in July, Mitsui Mining demanded repayment of loans it said it made to Izui at Mitsubishi's request and that Mitsubishi had promised to repay.
Mitsubishi Oil managing director Masayuki Matsushita, in a Thursday news conference, denied his company had conducted any transactions with Izui or had lent him any money.
The company has also denied allegations by Mitsui Mining, which belongs to the rival Mitsui group of companies, that it requested the funneling of funds to Izui.

Last week, the Osaka Taxation Bureau asked prosecutors to press tax evasion charges against Izui, alleging he had evaded 320 million yen in taxes by not reporting 660 million yen in income from 1992 to 1994.
